data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient to correlated failure than a large redundant service because it replaces 'hardware redundancy' with 'operational diversity', which breaks the single-plane failure mode.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services all rely on a single 'industry standard' library with a critical vulnerability (the 'Common Library Trap').","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The services share a common underlying infrastructure provider (e.g., all hosted on one cloud region).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The network lacks sufficient capacity to handle the redistribution of load when a subset of nodes fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a large service, internal redundancy (e.g., 100 identical nodes) is typically managed by a unified control plane or deployment pipeline. A single 'poison pill' configuration or orchestration bug creates a correlated failure across all redundant units. In a decentralized network, diverse deployment pipelines, different OS versions, and varied operator behaviors ensure that a single administrative or logical error has a limited 'blast radius', preventing total system collapse.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
